newsitem.title: USA: ABC, Discovery Channel to team up.
newsitem.headline: ABC, Discovery Channel to team up.

text.p: ABC News and cable television's Discovery Channel on Friday will begin telecasting a news show devoted exclusively to science, the companies announced Monday.

The programme, Discovery News, springs from the idea that science plays a role in many general news stories, from the investigation into last year's crash of TWA Flight 800 to last week's mass suicide of members of the Heaven's Gate cult, the companies said.
The Discovery News will begin airing Friday at 9 p.m. EST on the Discovery Channel, which is owned by Discovery Communications Inc., a unit of Englewood, Colo.-based Liberty Media Corp.
To underscore its high-tech nature, the show's anchor, Steve Aveson, won't even be working on a "real" set.

Instead, he'll be standing in a barren studio about 10 feet by 10 feet with a blue backdrop that a computer will turn into a "virtual" set that looks considerably larger. Viewers will see a room with the usual accoutrements found on a news set.

Besides offering a futuristic feel to the programme, the set is less expensive to create. The programming for the virtual set cost about $50,000, while a conventional set would have cost about $350,000.
"A show about science and technology should use science and technology," William Abrams, ABC News' vice president for business development and marketing, said at a news conference.
"You should think of it as a cross between (ABC's) 'World News Tonight' and Time magazine," said Carol Williams, the show's producer.

The two companies also will produce Discovery News Breaks, which will air nightly Sunday through Thursday on the Discovery Channel. They also will team up to produce live coverage of breaking news events, periodic one-hour specials and public opinion polls on science-related news.
